races.title: State House, District 23
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Patricia Smith
cands.bio: Accountant and small business owner from Williamston, NC. Ran for mayor of Williamston in 2023 and placed third. Defeated incumbent Rep. Shelly Willingham in the March 2026 Democratic primary and won the November 2026 general election for NC House District 23.

endorsements.text: Progressive Caucus of the North Carolina Democratic Party (also listed as recommended by several Sway voter-guide groups)

cands.gaps: We found no documented positions from Patricia Smith on data centers, development or growth, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor land buying, immigration or H-1B, policing, guns, or abortion. Her only stated policy priorities are education, economic development, healthcare and small-business concerns, including tariffs. We could not find the year she began her accounting career or the name of her business. Her exact birthplace is not stated beyond being a native of Williamston. She has no prior legislative record and no deeds in office to report.

local.label: Roots 100: She describes herself as a native of Williamston, NC, and graduated from Williamston High School, which suggests she was born and raised there.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Accountant serving North Carolina and surrounding states for over 40 years and a small business owner; ran for Williamston mayor in 2023 and lost. She has held no elected office.
qual.why: A long accounting career and business ownership fit the middle range (business owners and managers). She has no legislative service or elected office, so she scores below the high range.
qual.label: A long accounting career and business ownership fit the middle range (business owners and managers). She has no legislative service or elected office, so she scores below the high range.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: She said in her Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey that she is fighting for better pay for educators and for the public education system. She did not mention vouchers, charters or school choice.

prio.label: Matches 1 of 1 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 1 only promised (needs 2 to score)

roots.summary: She describes herself as a native of Williamston, NC, and graduated from Williamston High School, which suggests she was born and raised there.

cands.name: Brent Roberson
cands.bio: Business owner who describes himself as a logger and contractor. Born in Williamston, NC, with a 2023 NC State bachelor's degree... corrected: NC State bachelor's degree (1995). Republican candidate for NC House District 23 in 2024 and 2026, and for U.S. House District 1 in 2022. Has held no office.
cands.gaps: We found no state-level policy statements from Roberson for his 2024 or 2026 House races. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2024 or 2026 candidate surveys, and Ballotpedia lists no endorsements for him. His only stated positions come from his 2022 congressional campaign. We found nothing on his views about data centers, development, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor land ownership, school choice or teacher pay, or police pay. We could not confirm when he came to North Carolina, since he says he has always lived here, and we found no details on his business or its history beyond 'business owner', 'logger' and 'contractor'. We found no controversies and no foreign ties.

local.label: Roots 100: Ballotpedia lists Williamston, NC as his birthplace, and in a 2022 candidate survey he said he has lived and worked in the 1st Congressional District his whole life; the upbringing claim is self-reported.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Business owner; in 2022 he described himself as a logger and contractor who built businesses from the ground up. He has held no elected office and has no legislative, law or policy career on the record.
qual.why: Business ownership places him in the middle band for this office. He has no prior legislative service or policy or budget career.
qual.label: Business ownership places him in the middle band for this office. He has no prior legislative service or policy or budget career.

pro-life.evidence: Said on his 2022 U.S. House campaign website that he is firmly committed to protecting the lives of the unborn.

second-amendment.evidence: Said on his 2022 U.S. House campaign website that the Second Amendment 'shall not be infringed' and that he would fight to protect and expand gun rights.

workers-first.evidence: Said on his 2022 U.S. House campaign website that the border must be secured, the wall finished, and Border Patrol and ICE given the resources they need.
